question.problem:
Find the general solution to the system of differential equations given by

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=-6{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=3{x}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Given a decoupled system of first-order linear ODEs in the form

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118303/assets/630f2ae400ab4ccd212138703f93516384c23b284f5ecac5b8c459964f436d0b.svg)
the formula for the general solution is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118303/assets/fffb7d52ff1ec576d336b3498e40ea433546d971a398550848359cda657f957c.svg)

First, we write our differential equation in matrix form:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118303/assets/d5c965f4aa3a43689e92d60295049b1d7388c0d7eaf8b8ee93c1bd7eec4af207.svg)

Since the matrix of the differential system is diagonal, the system is decoupled.
